basic_info: 34-year-old female presenting with back pain for six days.
present_illness: Back pain started six days ago while walking, with a sudden seizure-like episode. The patient has been taking ibuprofen and using heat, but the pain remains stiff. The pain is in the lower back, and it feels pretty stiff. It is not on one side more than the other, and there is no numbness or tingling in the legs or feet. No changes in bowel or bladder function have been reported. The seizure-like episode was more like a sudden back spasm, not a true seizure, and occurred while walking. It was not associated with loss of consciousness and may have been related to increased activity or lifting weights. The pain has not radiated to the legs or feet and is worse with certain movements. The patient has been lifting weights a few times a week, which may have contributed to the symptoms. No prior episodes like this have been reported. The patient was walking, probably a bit faster than usual, and all of a sudden my back just clenched up on me. I wasn't sure if it was because of the pace or maybe because I had been lifting weights earlier that day. It felt like a spasm, and it happened pretty quickly. The pain is in my lower back, and it's been pretty constant, though it does feel worse when I move certain ways, like bending or extending my back. I haven't had any recent trauma, but I have been lifting weights a few times a week, so maybe that had something to do with it. No, I haven't had any numbness, tingling, or weakness in my legs, and my bowel and bladder functions haven't changed. I've been able to go about my normal activities, though the pain does make some movements uncomfortable. I do a lot of deadlifts, and I've been doing that about three times a week. I haven't really changed my form or the number of reps or sets, but I'm not sure if that's what caused the pain or if it was something else, like when I was walking faster than usual.
